## Section 6: Competitive Intelligence

**Basis and assumptions**
- Built only from the four competitor profiles and the competitive analysis provided. No web access was used.
- The company profile leaves "What they sell" and "Named competitors" blank. I assumed Acme Advisory is a solo AI consulting practice covering AI strategy, AI governance and ISO 42001 readiness, and AI sales enablement. Sam is the single senior advisor.
- Acme Advisory's pricing, client proof, and win/loss history were not provided. Every "we win" claim below is conditional on you confirming it.
- Competitors are described by category, not brand name.

---

### 1. Competitive Landscape Overview

#### Market map

| Category | Who they are | Threat type | Where they meet us |
|---|---|---|---|
| **The Global Network** | World's largest professional services network. US$70.5 billion revenue in fiscal 2025, 470,000+ people. | Indirect / incumbent | Enterprise AI governance, assurance, strategy, workforce change |
| **The Solo Senior Operator** | One named AI advisor and part-time Chief AI Officer. Capped at two concurrent fractional clients. | Direct | CEO and board AI strategy, governance, ISO 42001 readiness, workshops |
| **The Fractional C-Suite Platform** | Fractional executive firm with a part-time Chief AI Officer role among about 13 executive roles. | Direct / adjacent | Interim AI leadership, governance, AI sales enablement content |
| **The Compliance Specialist** | Cybersecurity and audit firm with its own compliance platform and an AI governance line. | Narrow / adjacent | ISO 42001 certification and audit readiness |

#### Market share and velocity
- **Market share:** Not available. No source gives share for AI advisory. Only scale figures exist, and they are not comparable across these firms.
- **Gaining traction (moves, not revenue):**
  - **Global Network:** Expanded AI controls and assurance services in August 2026. Cites a governance gap: 74% of companies plan to deploy agentic AI within two years, and 21% report mature agent governance.
  - **Solo Senior Operator:** Homepage updated 7 October 2026. Cut the consulting floor from USD 100,000 to USD 80,000 and the minimum from 100 to 80 hours. Heavy investment in search and AI-answer content.
  - **Fractional Platform:** Now features the AI officer as the only service in the homepage Services block. Pushes a shadow-AI survey (dated October 2025).
  - **Compliance Specialist:** AI is now central to its headline. It added AI chatbot testing, HITRUST for AI and ISO 42001 certification, and positions itself as a product company.
- **Losing relevance:** No competitor shows clear decline in the documents.
  - **Reputation risk, Global Network:** A 2025 government report refund tied to AI-generated errors sits awkwardly next to its "trustworthy AI" claim.
  - **Credibility risk, Solo Senior Operator:** Inconsistent pricing and claims across pages.
- **Read of the market:** Every competitor has moved toward AI governance in the past year. Governance is now crowded. Adoption, change and sales enablement are where the competitors are thinner.

### 2. Detailed Competitor Profiles

#### A. The Global Network (indirect / incumbent)

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Firmographics** | HQ London (US site is the main buyer-facing one). Private, member-firm structure, no listing or public funding. 470,000+ people. Serves nearly 90% of the Fortune 500, plus mid-market and family firms through a private-company unit. Industries: consumer, energy, financial services, government, life sciences and health care, technology, media and telecom. A FY2026 figure of US$74.5 billion appears only in an unverified blog. |
| **Core value proposition** | "Unlock the potential of AI while protecting what matters most." Claims teams move fast on AI but lack one defensible way to govern it. Warns against governing too little (risk) or too much (slows adoption). Category claimed: a branded trusted-AI framework. |
| **Product** | AI risk and governance program, AI controls and assurance, ISO 42001 readiness, workforce and change management, AI strategy and workshops. |
| **Pricing** | Custom, negotiated, project-based. No public rate card. Third-party estimates only: blended $200 to $800 per hour. A public-sector price sheet lists $373 per hour for an executive. A competing AI firm (biased) claims AI advisory starts around $250,000 and takes 6 to 18 months. No self-serve tier. |
| **GTM** | Enterprise relationships, cross-sell from audit and risk accounts, public RFP page, thought leadership, webcasts, press releases, alliance partners. Wins on brand safety, global scale, and bundled services. |

#### B. The Solo Senior Operator (direct)

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Firmographics** | HQ Prague, works remotely. Clients in the US, UK, EU and Middle East. Solo practitioner, capped at two concurrent fractional clients. He also leads two technology services companies (one 200+ specialists). Funding: not found. Targets mid-market and enterprise CEOs and boards. Industry pages: financial services, private equity, healthcare, ecommerce, technology. |
| **Core value proposition** | Homepage: "AI transformation consultant and fractional CAIO." Problem: AI pilots with no executive owner for priorities, funding and risk. An older page claimed a narrower category, "decision leverage above strategy." |
| **Product** | Part-time Chief AI Officer seat (about one day a week, up to 30 hours a month). Scoped consulting starting with a six-week readiness audit. Agentic AI advisory. Governance and ISO 42001 readiness (no certificates issued). Board advisory and workshops. |
| **Pricing** | Published. Consulting USD 1,000 per hour, 80-hour minimum, USD 80,000 floor. Seat USD 30,000 per month, six-month minimum, USD 180,000 minimum total. Workshops USD 50,000+. Engineering and specialists billed extra. |
| **GTM** | Inbound only. Search and AI-answer SEO is the main channel: buyer guides, "best consultant" lists, comparison pages that include himself (disclosed as first-party). Brief gets a reply in two business days. Business media council membership as a credibility signal. No events or partner channels found. |

#### C. The Fractional C-Suite Platform (direct / adjacent)

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Firmographics** | HQ Atlanta, with offices in several US cities and London. Private. Founded 2003 (one source says 2004). Headcount conflicts across its own pages: 125 partners plus 150 professionals, 245+ people, 240 employees. Funding: not found. Claims 7,000+ companies served, from startups to large enterprises. Targets growth-stage firms, boards, and private equity and venture firms. |
| **Core value proposition** | Headline: "Fractional Executives." AI message: "AI is already inside your business. Without leadership, it stays fragmented." Claims AI use is uncoordinated and ungoverned, and that most firms do not need a permanent Chief AI Officer. Category: the full fractional C-suite on one platform. |
| **Product** | Part-time Chief AI Officer plus an AI bench of architects and data specialists as needed. Covers use-case priorities, governance for data and model oversight, cross-team alignment, interim leadership and handover. Recent content on AI sales enablement and generative-search marketing. |
| **Pricing** | Retainer model, not published. A third party estimates $12,000 to $30,000 a month. That figure comes from a fractional CTO cost guide, so it is only a rough proxy. Claims up to 75% less than a full-time hire. No AI-specific pricing found. |
| **GTM** | Sales-led. Main call to action is a 15-minute call. Free guides, an AI usage survey, case studies, steady blog output. Embeds operating partners in private equity portfolio companies. Wins on long track record, bench breadth, and "operators, not consultants." |

#### D. The Compliance Specialist (narrow / adjacent)

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Firmographics** | HQ New Jersey, with offices in Toronto and Bengaluru. Private, unfunded per one tracker. Says 100+ experts. A tracker lists 139 staff. Self-reports 450+ clients and 96% retention. Founding year and revenue conflict across sources, so treat both as unverified. Industries: finance, health, manufacturing, media, retail, software, public sector, venture and private equity. Appears to serve small and mid-size software, health and fintech teams. |
| **Core value proposition** | "Human-Led Expertise. AI-Powered Efficiency. Product-Driven Trust." Claims to move buyers from point-in-time audits to continuous compliance visibility, and to remove the need for multiple vendors. |
| **Product** | Audits and certification readiness (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HITRUST and others), multi-framework bundle, proprietary compliance platform, penetration testing including AI chatbot testing, outsourced security leadership, staffing. ISO 42001 support with auditors on staff. |
| **Pricing** | Custom quotes. Promises upfront pricing on its SOC 2 bundle but shows no number. Entry price not found. Independent guides put first-year ISO 27001 at $17,500 to $100,000, which is market context, not this firm's price. |
| **GTM** | Expert-led sales ("Speak To An Expert," "Book A Demo"). Services first, platform pulled in through the engagement. Large SEO library including "best consultants" posts. Case studies, awards, partner channels. Wins where the buyer needs a certificate or audit report. |

### 3. Comparative SWOT (relative to Acme Advisory)

#### A. The Global Network

| Category | Description |
|:---|:---|
| **Strengths** | Brand safety: "nobody gets fired for choosing us." Global scale, alliances, bundled audit, risk and consulting. Credible with boards, regulators and large buyers. Ranked first in its category by revenue. |
| **Weaknesses** | No public pricing or scope before a sales call. Enterprise-shaped offer with no stated option for small or mid-size executive teams. Long, project-heavy timelines (a competitor claim, unverified). Audit independence rules limit some services for audit clients. A documented, widely covered AI error and fee refund undercuts its trust claim. The AI pages do not name who leads the work. |
| **Opportunities (For Us)** | Buyers who want a named senior advisor working directly, not a staffed team. Buyers who need a result in weeks, not a multi-month program. Mid-size firms that are too small to get senior attention. Use the refund case as a quality-control question, not an attack. |
| **Threats (To Us)** | Can bundle AI governance into audit renewals at low marginal cost. Can win any deal where procurement demands a large, insured vendor. Its new assurance services tie AI governance to financial reporting, which pulls regulated buyers toward it. |

#### B. The Solo Senior Operator

| Category | Description |
|:---|:---|
| **Strengths** | Same one-named-advisor model as ours. Published fees, which lower buyer friction. Honest scope limits (no certificates, no build work). Strong search and AI-answer presence. Industry pages for private equity, health and finance. Reports running AI in companies he leads. |
| **Weaknesses** | Two-client capacity cap. High entry cost: USD 80,000 consulting floor and USD 180,000 seat minimum. Seat is up to 30 hours a month. Case results shown belong to his companies, not his consulting, and named AI client references were not found. Related-party risk: he leads software firms that could build what he recommends. Price terms differ across pages. Broad offer (marketing, search, fractional CTO) dilutes the message. |
| **Opportunities (For Us)** | Buyers below his floor or unwilling to commit six months. Buyers who want a bounded engagement, not a seat. Buyers who need hands-on staff adoption, not only board-level decisions. Buyers who want advice with no implementation stake. Verifiable named client proof, if we have it, is a clear gap on his side. |
| **Threats (To Us)** | His comparison pages and "best consultant" lists shape what buyers and AI assistants see first. His floor has already fallen once and may fall again. His ISO 42001 readiness page competes directly with our governance work. He openly pits himself against global networks, which sharpens the "senior operator over big bench" story we also tell. |

#### C. The Fractional C-Suite Platform

| Category | Description |
|:---|:---|
| **Strengths** | Longest track record in the fractional model. Broad bench across every executive role. Can place AI next to finance, technology and revenue roles. Private equity embedding gives it a repeat channel. Moving fast to put AI at the front of its site. |
| **Weaknesses** | AI is one of about 13 roles. AI team entries show no AI-specific credentials on the page reviewed. No public pricing. Partners work independently, so quality can vary (third-party view). No standards-based governance path (no ISO 42001 mention found). Change management and staff training are not the focus. AI proof is thin: 20+ case studies are listed but none were verified as AI work. Size claims conflict. |
| **Opportunities (For Us)** | AI-first depth against a generalist bench. Buyers who want a certification path and a defined governance standard. Buyers who need staff adoption and training. Clear, named accountability against a partner network where the person you meet may not be the person who delivers. |
| **Threats (To Us)** | Can offer AI leadership as an add-on to existing finance or technology retainers. Existing relationships with boards and private equity sponsors. Can add AI specialists quickly through its bench. Its AI sales and generative-search content overlaps with our sales enablement offer. |

#### D. The Compliance Specialist

| Category | Description |
|:---|:---|
| **Strengths** | Audit and testing under one roof, plus its own platform. Large client base (self-reported). Strong search content. Accredited audit capability that a solo advisor cannot match. Clear fit when a buyer needs a certificate or report. |
| **Weaknesses** | No AI strategy, executive coaching, change management or AI sales enablement offer. AI governance is framed as certification and security. A customer quote on its own site admits the standard "is new enough that most firms are learning it on your dime." Delivery team is not named. Pricing not public. Employee reviews are weak (2.6 out of 5), which is a possible delivery risk signal, not buyer feedback. Stats vary by page. |
| **Opportunities (For Us)** | Buyers who ask "what should we do with AI?" before "how do we get certified?" Buyers who need leadership alignment and staff adoption alongside governance. Partner role: we shape the program, a specialist audits. |
| **Threats (To Us)** | Owns the certification step, which is the end point many governance buyers want. Can bundle ISO 42001 with other frameworks at a lower combined cost. Pulls buyers into platform use, which raises switching costs. |

### 4. "How to Win" (Battlecard Summary)

| Competitor | When we win | When they win |
|---|---|---|
| **The Global Network** | The buyer is a mid-size company that wants a named senior advisor, a short engagement, and a visible price before committing. We are the obvious choice when speed and direct access matter more than brand cover. | The buyer is a large or regulated enterprise, procurement requires a big vendor, or AI governance is tied to audit and financial reporting. Expect heavy resistance. Do not compete on scale or insurance. |
| **The Solo Senior Operator** | The buyer is below his price floor, wants a bounded engagement, wants no advisor-owned implementation interest, or needs hands-on adoption work with staff. We win on fit and independence, if Acme Advisory confirms those facts. | The buyer wants a board-level Chief AI Officer seat and can pay USD 180,000 or more, or finds him first through search. Be careful: he also sells "one named senior advisor," so that line is not a unique edge. Do not attack his published pricing. |
| **The Fractional C-Suite Platform** | The buyer wants AI-specific depth, a standards-based governance path, and one accountable person rather than a rotating bench. We win when AI is the main problem, not one of several executive gaps. | The buyer already uses its finance, technology or revenue executives, or a private equity sponsor has placed it in the portfolio. Expect resistance where one vendor for all fractional roles is the goal. |
| **The Compliance Specialist** | The buyer needs AI strategy, leadership alignment and adoption before any audit. We are the obvious choice when the question is "where should AI go and how do we get people to use it safely?" | The buyer has a customer or regulator asking for a certificate or audit report now. We cannot issue one, so lead with a partner model rather than competing head-on. |
